artifact.self_contained_problem:
Background and definitions. Let A be a finite alphabet. Two finite words u, v over A are abelian equivalent if v is a permutation of u, i.e. each letter of A occurs the same number of times in u and v. For a real number s > 1 with s = k + f where k is a positive integer and 0 ≤ f < 1, an abelian s-power is a word of the form x_1 x_2 … x_k y, where x_1, …, x_k are pairwise abelian equivalent nonempty words of the same length |x_i| = m, and y is an abelian-equivalent prefix-style factor of length ⌊f·m⌋ that is abelian equivalent to a prefix of x_1 of that length. A word w is said to encounter an abelian s-power if some factor of w is an abelian s-power; otherwise w avoids abelian s-powers. More generally, given a pattern p (a word over a set of variables), a word w over A encounters p in the abelian sense if there is a non-erasing morphism h, with the convention that the images of equal variables are abelian equivalent (rather than equal), such that h(p) is a factor of w; otherwise w avoids p in the abelian sense.

Let Z_n denote the set of all infinite words over an n-letter alphabet, and say that Z_n encounters p in the abelian sense if every infinite word over n letters encounters p in the abelian sense.

Define on the interval (1, 2] the abelian repetitive threshold function
  ART(n) = inf { s ∈ (1, 2] : abelian s-powers are avoidable over an n-letter alphabet by some infinite word },
and the dual abelian repetitive threshold function
  DART(r) = min { n ∈ ℕ : abelian r-powers are avoidable over an n-letter alphabet by some infinite word }.

Problems.
(a) Determine the computational complexity of the following decision problem: given a pattern p and a positive integer n, decide whether Z_n encounters p in the abelian sense.
(b) Determine the values of ART(n) for every integer n ≥ 2, and determine the values of DART(r) for every r ∈ (1, 2].
artifact.status_search_result: The abelian repetition threshold problem remains an active open area: only partial values are known (e.g., bounds on the abelian repetition threshold for small alphabets), and the general values of ART(n) and DART(r), as well as the complexity of deciding abelian encounter of a pattern over an n-letter alphabet, do not appear to be settled. Surveys and follow-up works continue to list these as open.

status_evidence.title: On abelian repetition threshold
status_evidence.snippet: The main goal in this paper is to find an Abelian analogue of the repetition threshold... numerical value separating k-avoidable and k-unavoidable Abelian powers for each alphabet size k.
status_evidence.claim: The abelian repetition threshold is only partially known; general values remain open.

status_evidence.title: Abelian Complexity in Minimal Subshifts
status_evidence.snippet: Research addresses limitations of usual, fractional, abelian, and k-abelian repetitions and other generalizations such as patterns and formulas.
status_evidence.claim: Abelian pattern avoidance and thresholds remain an active research direction with open questions.
